description: Shared cross-language test vectors for the ato.capsule-program/v1 canonical form (ADR-014 §9: contract/ + manifest/ + source/ suites). Consumed by crates/capsule/tests/capsule_program_vectors.rs and reusable verbatim by a second-language implementation (Phase 1).
manifest_suite_pipeline: Each manifest/vectors/*.toml is written to an otherwise-empty source root (plus the side files listed in the harness setup: model-sha256-* and reject-engine-path materialize model.gguf), loaded with the ordinary v0.3 normalizer (load_manifest, strict validation), then adapted with program_intent_from_v03. expect=intent vectors must equal their expected_file JSON exactly; vectors sharing one expected_file are equivalent authored spellings of the same declaration. expect=error vectors must fail (at either pipeline stage) with a message containing error_substring.
source_projection_suite: Each source/vectors/<name>/ directory is a committed, regular-files-only fixture tree. Freeze it with materialize_source_archive into a content-addressed .tar.zst and mint the pinned source materialization by extracting that archive with from_source_archive (the only public mint; no directory is self-attested), run the ProgramSourceProjectionV1 derivation over the extracted root (A1v2 admissibility, staging copy, resolve the control files at the selected root, exclude exactly those paths), and compare: the remaining files must equal projected_files (paths relative to the vector root, '/'-joined, lexicographically sorted) and the A1 tree hash of that projection must equal source_digest. relation is measured against source_baseline. Symlink and executable-bit scenarios are deliberately NOT committed here (they do not survive every platform/VCS checkout) — see README.md for the unit tests that cover them.

contract_vectors.name: field-order
contract_vectors.notes: same contract with every object's keys reverse-sorted; JCS erases key order, so canonical bytes and id equal the baseline's exactly

contract_vectors.name: mutate-source-digest
contract_vectors.notes: one hex digit of the pinned A1 source digest differs; the id must change

contract_vectors.name: mutate-intent
contract_vectors.notes: manifest_intent.capsule_type differs; declaration intent is identity-bearing

contract_vectors.name: invalid-unknown-top-level
contract_vectors.notes: unknown top-level identity-bearing field fails closed (deny_unknown_fields)

contract_vectors.name: invalid-unknown-intent-field
contract_vectors.notes: unknown field inside manifest_intent fails closed — non-identity manifest data (e.g. name) must never deserialize into the intent

contract_vectors.name: invalid-schema-string
contract_vectors.notes: contract schema version mismatch fails validate() closed

contract_vectors.name: invalid-source-digest-blake3
contract_vectors.notes: a blake3-spelled ProgramSourceDigest is rejected on typed parse: the A1 source tree hash is sha256-only

contract_vectors.name: invalid-duplicate-state-key
contract_vectors.notes: a duplicate key in a top-level identity map (state) is rejected by the unique-map deserializer: BTreeMap last-wins would give two byte-distinct documents one id

contract_vectors.name: invalid-duplicate-nested-env-key
contract_vectors.notes: a duplicate key in a NESTED identity map (targets.<label>.env) is rejected too — the fail-closed rule is not only top level

contract_vectors.name: envelope-non-identity-b
contract_vectors.notes: same contract as envelope-non-identity-a with different generated_at/provenance/diagnostics and a tolerated unknown envelope field; verify() passes and the verified id is identical

contract_vectors.name: envelope-id-mismatch
contract_vectors.notes: stored capsule_program_id disagrees with the canonical hash of program_contract; readers fail closed

manifest_vectors.name: baseline-oci
manifest_vectors.notes: the BASE-style app manifest: one named OCI target

manifest_vectors.name: equivalent-metadata-change
manifest_vectors.notes: differs from baseline-oci only in name/version/[metadata]/[routing]/[pool] (non-identity + excluded sections): shares baseline-oci's expected intent file

manifest_vectors.name: source-run-alias
manifest_vectors.notes: aliases (target run=, service command=) plus authored explicit-default sections ([snapshot] mode=none, empty [network]/[pack]): canonicalizes into the same IR as the canonical spelling

manifest_vectors.name: source-run-canonical
manifest_vectors.notes: the canonical spelling of the same declaration as source-run-alias

manifest_vectors.name: web-root-entrypoint
manifest_vectors.notes: web static target with working_dir = ".": the IR pins the canonical Root spelling {"source_relative": "."}

manifest_vectors.name: model-sha256-bare
manifest_vectors.notes: bare-hex model_sha256 authoring spelling; model is a SourceExistingPath (the harness materializes model.gguf)

manifest_vectors.name: model-sha256-prefixed
manifest_vectors.notes: sha256:-prefixed model_sha256 authoring spelling; normalizes into the same IR (bare lowercase hex) as model-sha256-bare

manifest_vectors.name: wasm-world-default
manifest_vectors.notes: structured [targets.wasm] with world authored absent: the IR pins the default-expanded "wasi:cli/command"

manifest_vectors.name: oci-user
manifest_vectors.notes: user = "1000:1000" is a valid ContainerUserSpec and stays visible in the IR

manifest_vectors.name: seal-at
manifest_vectors.notes: [seal_at] is identity-bearing authored verification intent (same category as [snapshot]): the argv is hashed as OpaqueCommand elements with argument boundaries exact — an explicitly selected shell, a space-containing argument kept as ONE element, and a trailing empty argument preserved

manifest_vectors.name: reject-workspace
manifest_vectors.notes: workspace manifests fail Program Identity issuance closed (ADR-014 Phase 0)

manifest_vectors.name: reject-engine-path
manifest_vectors.notes: engine_path names a host-local binary; it can never be part of a portable declaration (Rule 3)

manifest_vectors.name: reject-unknown-top-level
manifest_vectors.notes: the tolerant model parser silently drops unknown top-level keys; the strict identity gate rejects them instead of hashing around dropped authoring

manifest_vectors.name: reject-source-digest-bare
manifest_vectors.notes: targets.source_digest requires the sha256: prefix (existing validator); the bare spelling is rejected before the adapter runs

source_vectors.name: baseline
source_vectors.notes: manifest + two ordinary source files, no lock: the root capsule.toml is excluded and everything else is hashed

source_vectors.name: with-canonical-lock
source_vectors.notes: baseline's source bytes plus a root capsule.lock: the resolved lock never reaches the preimage, so the digest is the baseline's exactly (fixed point)

source_vectors.name: with-deprecated-alias-lock
source_vectors.notes: baseline's source bytes plus a root ato.lock.json: the deprecated alias resolves to the same single excluded lock path, so the digest survives the lock-file rename

source_vectors.name: nested-control-names
source_vectors.notes: baseline's source bytes plus examples/capsule.toml and fixtures/capsule.lock: only the SELECTED ROOT's control files are special, so both nested files are ordinary source, stay in the projected set, and change the digest (exact-path rule, no content sniffing)

source_vectors.name: nested-dir-tree
source_vectors.notes: nested directories plus sibling names that sort across the '/' boundary (a.txt / a/ / ab/): pins recursion and the A1 child-ordering rule
